title: Influence of Increased TaNbV on the Microstructure, Mechanical Properties, and Energy Release Characteristics of High-Entropy Alloy HfZrTi(TaNbV)<sub>x</sub>.

recollection.starting_material: An equimolar Hf–Zr–Ti high-entropy alloy base
recollection.intervention: Incremental additions of a Ta–Nb–V refractory element mixture at different x levels (e.g. x = 0.1, 0.2, 0.3), prepared by arc-melting and homogenization
recollection.structure: Predominantly single-phase body-centered cubic (BCC) solid solution with a slight increase in lattice parameter and the onset of minute Ta–Nb–V–rich clusters or secondary phase particles at the highest x
recollection.mechanism: Extra lattice distortion and solid-solution strengthening from the larger Ta, Nb, and V atoms, combined with increased chemical short-range order, which raises both the static strength and the stored elastic energy available for rapid release
recollection.results: With x increasing to ∼0.3–0.4, yield strength rose from ~800 MPa to ~1,200 MPa, Vickers hardness climbed from ~3.5 GPa to ~5.0 GPa, and measured energy-release density in a standard dynamical test improved by ~10 % compared to the x = 0 baseline (guess)

score.note: The recollection correctly identifies graded Ta–Nb–V additions to equimolar Hf–Zr–Ti, but gives incorrect composition levels and processing. It misses the HCP→BCC transition and omega phase, instead inventing clusters/particles. Lattice-distortion and solid-solution strengthening are broadly correct, while short-range order and stored elastic energy are unsupported. The reported strengths, composition range, hardness, and energy-release improvement do not match the paper.
